items.question: How many departments are there in each department group? Show the group name and the count.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) GroupName,
                   COUNT(*) AS DepartmentCount
FROM HumanResources.Department
GROUP BY GroupName
ORDER BY DepartmentCount DESC
items.answer:
There are 6 department groups. The counts are:

- Executive General and Administration: 5
- Research and Development: 3
- Sales and Marketing: 2
- Inventory Management: 2
- Manufacturing: 2

The result was cut off at 5 rows shown, so the sixth group's count isn't visible here — see the full results table next to this answer for that last row.

items.question: What is the average standard cost of the products that have a standard cost above zero?
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) AVG(StandardCost) AS AvgStandardCost,
                   COUNT(*) AS ProductCount
FROM Production.Product
WHERE StandardCost > 0
items.answer: The average standard cost of products with a standard cost above zero is 428.7364, based on 304 products.

items.question: How many order lines were sold with a special offer other than the 'No Discount' offer?
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) COUNT(*) AS OrderLineCount
FROM Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS d
     INNER JOIN
     Sales.SpecialOffer AS s
     ON s.SpecialOfferID = d.SpecialOfferID
WHERE s.Description <> 'No Discount'
items.answer: 5,433 order lines were sold with a special offer other than 'No Discount'.

items.question: For each sales reason, how many sales orders cite it? Show the reason name and the order count.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) r.Name AS ReasonName,
                   COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeaderSalesReason AS sr
     INNER JOIN
     Sales.SalesReason AS r
     ON r.SalesReasonID = sr.SalesReasonID
GROUP BY r.Name
ORDER BY OrderCount DESC
items.answer:
Here are the order counts per sales reason (top rows shown; the full list of 7 reasons is in the results table):

Price: 17,473 orders
On Promotion: 3,515 orders
Manufacturer: 1,746 orders
Quality: 1,551 orders
Other: 1,395 orders

The remaining two reasons are in the results table next to this answer.

items.question: How many sales orders were placed in the last quarter of 2013 (October to December)?
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader
WHERE OrderDate >= '2013-10-01'
      AND OrderDate < '2014-01-01'
items.answer:
6,121 sales orders were placed in the last quarter of 2013 (October 1 – December 31, 2013).

⚠ some figures could not be verified against the results

items.question: How many orders in my territory have an order total (TotalDue) above the average order total of my territory?
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) COUNT(*) AS OrdersAboveAvg
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS h
WHERE h.TotalDue > (SELECT AVG(h2.TotalDue)
                    FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS h2
                    WHERE h2.TerritoryID = h.TerritoryID)
items.answer: 554 orders in your territory have a TotalDue above your territory's average order total.

items.question: Which products have more than 2 records in their standard cost history? Show the product ID and the number of records.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) ProductID,
                   COUNT(*) AS RecordCount
FROM Production.ProductCostHistory
GROUP BY ProductID
HAVING COUNT(*) > 2
ORDER BY RecordCount DESC, ProductID
items.answer: 25 products have more than 2 records in their standard cost history. Each of them has exactly 3 records — the highest count in the result. The first few product IDs are 707, 708, 711, 712 and 713; the full list is in the results table next to this answer.

items.question: Which job titles are held by more than 5 current employees (CurrentFlag = 1)? Show the job title and the number of employees.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) JobTitle,
                   COUNT(*) AS EmployeeCount
FROM HumanResources.Employee
WHERE CurrentFlag = 1
GROUP BY JobTitle
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5
ORDER BY EmployeeCount DESC
items.answer: Nine job titles are held by more than 5 current employees. The largest groups are Production Technician - WC40, WC50 and WC60 with 26 employees each, followed by WC30 with 25 and WC20 with 22. The remaining four titles are in the results table below.

items.question: Which 5 stores in my territory placed the most sales orders? Show the store name and the order count, highest first. Only count orders of store customers.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP 5 s.Name AS StoreName,
             COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS h
     INNER JOIN
     Sales.Customer AS c
     ON c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
     INNER JOIN
     Sales.Store AS s
     ON s.BusinessEntityID = c.StoreID
GROUP BY s.Name
ORDER BY OrderCount DESC
items.answer:
The 5 stores in your territory with the most sales orders (store customers only):

1. Central Discount Store — 12 orders
2. Great Bikes — 12 orders
3. Latest Sports Equipment — 12 orders
4. Moderately-Priced Bikes Store — 12 orders
5. Thorough Parts and Repair Services — 12 orders

All five are tied at 12 orders each.

items.question: How many different orders in my territory include at least one product from the 'Bikes' product category?
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) COUNT(DISTINCT h.SalesOrderID) AS BikeOrderCount
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS h
     INNER JOIN
     Sales.SalesOrderDetail AS d
     ON d.SalesOrderID = h.SalesOrderID
     INNER JOIN
     Production.Product AS p
     ON p.ProductID = d.ProductID
     INNER JOIN
     Production.ProductSubcategory AS s
     ON s.ProductSubcategoryID = p.ProductSubcategoryID
     INNER JOIN
     Production.ProductCategory AS c
     ON c.ProductCategoryID = s.ProductCategoryID
WHERE c.Name = 'Bikes'
items.answer: In your territory, 2,340 different orders include at least one product from the 'Bikes' category.

items.question: Who are the 5 individual customers (not stores) in my territory with the highest total order value (TotalDue)? Show first name, last name and the total, highest first.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP 5 p.FirstName,
             p.LastName,
             SUM(h.TotalDue) AS TotalOrderValue
FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader AS h
     INNER JOIN
     Sales.Customer AS c
     ON c.CustomerID = h.CustomerID
     INNER JOIN
     Person.Person AS p
     ON p.BusinessEntityID = c.PersonID
WHERE c.PersonID IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.FirstName, p.LastName
ORDER BY TotalOrderValue DESC
items.answer:
The 5 individual customers in your territory with the highest total order value (TotalDue):

1. Roger Harui — 989,184.08
2. Lindsey Camacho — 834,475.93
3. Richard Bready — 815,914.25
4. François Ferrier — 789,884.29
5. Margaret Vanderkamp — 650,362.05

Stores were excluded (only customers with a PersonID are included).

items.question: How many units are in stock per product category (the sum of Quantity in the product inventory, over all locations)? Show the category name and the quantity. Only count products that belong to a subcategory.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) c.Name AS Category,
                   SUM(i.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity
FROM Production.ProductInventory AS i
     INNER JOIN
     Production.Product AS p
     ON p.ProductID = i.ProductID
     INNER JOIN
     Production.ProductSubcategory AS s
     ON s.ProductSubcategoryID = p.ProductSubcategoryID
     INNER JOIN
     Production.ProductCategory AS c
     ON c.ProductCategoryID = s.ProductCategoryID
GROUP BY c.Name
ORDER BY TotalQuantity DESC
items.answer:
Units in stock per product category (products with a subcategory only):

Components: 47,214
Bikes: 15,536
Accessories: 9,128
Clothing: 5,940

items.question: Which 5 products have the largest total rejected quantity (RejectedQty) on purchase order lines? Show the product name and the total rejected quantity, highest first.

items.question: For each salesperson, what is their most recent sales quota in the quota history? Show the salesperson's last name, the quota date and the quota amount (SalesQuota).
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) p.LastName,
                   q.QuotaDate,
                   q.SalesQuota
FROM Sales.SalesPersonQuotaHistory AS q
     INNER JOIN
     Person.Person AS p
     ON p.BusinessEntityID = q.BusinessEntityID
WHERE q.QuotaDate = (SELECT MAX(q2.QuotaDate)
                     FROM Sales.SalesPersonQuotaHistory AS q2
                     WHERE q2.BusinessEntityID = q.BusinessEntityID)
ORDER BY p.LastName
items.answer:
Here are the most recent quotas for each salesperson (17 salespeople in total; the results table shows all rows).

The latest quota date for every salesperson is 2014-03-01. Examples from the results: Abbas 26,000.00, Alberts 1,000.00, Ansman-Wolfe 390,000.00, Blythe 869,000.00, Campbell 403,000.00. See the results table for the remaining salespeople.

items.question: What is the average current hourly pay rate per job title? Use each employee's most recent rate (the latest RateChangeDate) in the pay history. Show the job title and the average rate.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) e.JobTitle,
                   AVG(latest.Rate) AS AvgRate
FROM HumanResources.Employee AS e
     INNER JOIN
     (SELECT p.BusinessEntityID,
             p.Rate
      FROM HumanResources.EmployeePayHistory AS p
      WHERE p.RateChangeDate = (SELECT MAX(p2.RateChangeDate)
                                FROM HumanResources.EmployeePayHistory AS p2
                                WHERE p2.BusinessEntityID = p.BusinessEntityID)) AS latest
     ON latest.BusinessEntityID = e.BusinessEntityID
GROUP BY e.JobTitle
ORDER BY AvgRate DESC
items.answer:
Here are the average current hourly pay rates per job title, based on each employee's most recent rate in the pay history (67 job titles in total, sorted highest first):

- Chief Executive Officer: 125.50
- Vice President of Production: 84.13
- Vice President of Sales: 72.12
- Vice President of Engineering: 63.46
- Chief Financial Officer: 60.10

The full list of all 67 job titles is in the results table next to this answer.

items.question: How many customers placed their first-ever sales order in each year? Show the year and the number of customers.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) YEAR(FirstOrderDate) AS FirstOrderYear,
                   COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount
FROM (SELECT CustomerID,
             MIN(OrderDate) AS FirstOrderDate
      FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader
      GROUP BY CustomerID) AS f
GROUP BY YEAR(FirstOrderDate)
ORDER BY FirstOrderYear
items.answer:
Here is the number of customers who placed their first-ever sales order in each year:

2011: 1,406 customers
2012: 2,961 customers
2013: 8,730 customers
2014: 6,022 customers

Each customer is counted once, in the year of their earliest order.

items.question: How many employees were hired in each year, and how many have been hired in total up to and including that year? Show the year, that year's hires and the cumulative total, in year order. Count every row of the employee table, including employees who are no longer current.
items.agentSql:
SELECT TOP (10001) YEAR(HireDate) AS HireYear,
                   COUNT(*) AS Hires,
                   SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (ORDER BY YEAR(HireDate)) AS CumulativeHires
FROM HumanResources.Employee
GROUP BY YEAR(HireDate)
ORDER BY HireYear
items.answer:
Here are the hires by year with the running total (all 290 employee rows, including former employees):

2006: 1 hire, cumulative 1
2007: 6 hires, cumulative 7
2008: 74 hires, cumulative 81
2009: 148 hires, cumulative 229
2010: 38 hires, cumulative 267

The result set has 8 year rows in total; the remaining years are shown in the results table next to this answer.
